subject: Post-demo: mode prioritization, constraints, and cutover checklist
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@medscribe.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: mode prioritization, constraints, and cutover checklist

Alex / Samira — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a short list of asks so we can finalize a recommended deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

Summary from call:
- Goal: replace VendorAI endpoints and retire our legacy GPU cluster while preserving the current 99th-pt latency SLO (~150ms) and supporting up to ~800 RPS during peak daily bursts.
- Data posture: PHI + PII in inference payloads; team prefers customer-controlled keys and VPC peering.
- Procurement: target decision window is Jan 2027; legal has started initial review.

Immediate asks to validate mode recommendation:
1) Confirm whether Medscribe requires an on-premise air-gapped option, or if a VPC-private deployment is sufficient.
2) Provide sample request/response payload sizes and typical sequence lengths (avg and 95th percentile).
3) Share current burst profile (minute-level vs sustained) and whether you need steady autoscale vs reserved throughput.

Our recommendation (prelim): based on PHI and required control over keys, a Dedicated pool with Private control plane (VPC) looks safest for predictable throughput and isolation. We also see a common two-step path: short Hosted POC for functional verification + Dedicated cutover for production throughput & compliance.

Attachments: redwood-mode-comparison.pdf (high-level tradeoffs), I can drop a cutover checklist once we get your payload/traffic numbers.

Next steps: can we get the three items above by EOD Monday (11/29)? If yes, I’ll loop in our Solutions Engineering lead and draft a canary plan.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
Note: attachment stub: redwood-mode-comparison.pdf (pdf, 420KB)
From: Alex Park <alex.park@medscribe.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@medscribe.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: mode prioritization, constraints, and cutover checklist

Michael — thanks for the crisp recap. Quick answers inline: 

1) On-prem air-gap: not required today. We need VPC peering + customer-managed KMS.
2) Payloads: average request ~2.8KB (text only), 95th pct ~9KB; responses avg ~1.2KB. Typical sequence length ~220 tokens avg, 95th ~1,100 tokens for long reports.
3) Traffic: baseline 120 RPS, predictable morning and evening spikes to ~800 RPS for ~10–15 minutes. We can tolerate short throttling during spikes if we have graceful fallback, but prefer reserved capacity for core workflows.

Other context:
- Migration source: we’re currently running VendorAI’s hosted endpoints; also have an internal GPU cluster (on-prem, NVIDIA A100s) used for backfill. Plan is to shift online traffic away from the cluster.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; legal wants evidence of audit logs and key controls.
- Procurement: budget signoff targeted by 2/10/2027; technical PO to engineering expected mid-Jan.

I’m attaching an excerpt of our API spec and a simple cost model we use. Can you and your team confirm whether the Dedicated + Private approach will meet the 150ms 99th SLO (with the token sizes above) and what the expected monthly committed cost would look like for the reserved profile?

Thanks,
Alex Park
Head of ML Infrastructure | Medscribe
alex.park@medscribe.com

---
Attachment stubs: medscribe-current_api_spec.json, medscribe-cost_model_v2.xlsx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@medscribe.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: mode prioritization, constraints, and cutover checklist

Alex — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. High level on cost and fit: 
- Dedicated + Private control plane is the clean fit given PHI + KMS needs. It gives predictable tail latency and isolation for your peak bursts.
- Hosting POC: we recommend a 2-week Hosted functional POC (no PHI residency) using synthetic data to validate model outputs, then a 4-week Dedicated POC with VPC to validate latency and autoscale.
- Pricing: I’ll send a reserved-capacity quote that maps to your baseline (120 RPS) + burst headroom; expect a discount at 12-month commit vs month-to-month.

We can also propose an interim hybrid: route non-sensitive traffic to Hosted while onboarding sensitive traffic into Dedicated. If legal needs SOC2 artifacts, we have an evidence package we can provide (audit logs, access control matrix).

Aditya
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@medscribe.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: mode prioritization, constraints, and cutover checklist

Alex — a few follow-ups to make the Dedicated POC planning crisp: 
- Can you export a 24-hour minute-level RPS sample (CSV) so we can size instance pools and warm caches?
- For the 95th token lengths (1,100 tokens), do you expect those calls to be synchronous customer-facing or async background jobs? If synchronous, we’ll model tail latency differently.
- Canary plan: we typically do a 3-stage cutover: 1) shadow traffic, 2) 5% canary for 48h with detailed tracing, 3) progressive ramp to 100% over 7 days. Is that acceptable?

Who should I loop in from your infra/ops team for the VPC peering and KMS exchange? Also, we’ll prepare a short checklist for your security team (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, retention policy).

If you can drop the sample RPS and confirm sync vs async by EOD Monday (11/29), I’ll assemble the POC runbook and proposed reserved sizing.

—
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@medscribe.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@medscribe.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: mode prioritization, constraints, and cutover checklist

Michael / Aditya — looping in Samira (ops) to answer network questions and confirming the asks:
- We attached the 24-hour minute-level traffic CSV and a sanitized API spec. (See medscribe-current_api_spec.json and medscribe-cost_model_v2.xlsx)
- Most long requests are synchronous (report generation endpoint), but we can convert a subset to async if needed.
- Ops contact for peering: Samira Khan (samira@medscribe.com), CCed here.
- Legal: we asked for a SOC2 evidence package; please point us to the specific artifacts needed (audit logs, config snapshots, KMS rotation policies).

We’re comfortable starting with Hosted POC for functionality, then move to Dedicated + Private for production. Please share the POC runbook and reserved sizing by Tue (12/1) if possible so procurement can start internal approvals.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Infrastructure Lead | Medscribe
